meaning: The comment claims Rvvs_v is the key fitted parameter because brain.out feeds Rijvs and Rvvs in parallel, so at Rvvs 0.04 mmHg/(mL/s) closing the jugular only diverts flow, giving +0.25 mmHg ICP instead of the patient's +10.24. It justifies fitting Rvvs_v rather than fixing it.

could_move.what: The quoted default-case numbers (+0.25 vs +10.24 mmHg, Rijvs.A 1.254 -> 0.191, 85% collapse, Rvvs 0.04) live only in prose; if model defaults or the tube law change, the comment stays as the stated argument while being wrong.

The parallel/series topology claim (Rijvs and Rvvs in parallel off brain.out; Rt and the Rivp/Revp/Razy chain downstream of Rvvs) decides which knob is fitted. If connectivity differs, Rvvs_v absorbs error belonging elsewhere.
P_jc_amp is fitted too and is unrecorded, so the two can trade off; attributing the ICP gap mainly to Rvvs_v may not be identifiable from these recordings.
All twelve jugular_compression decks consume the fitted m5 parameters, so a changed Rvvs_v shifts every M1/M4/M6 vs M5 comparison at once.

expectation: Direction: a larger Rvvs_v makes the vertebral route costlier, so compression should raise ICP more. Size unknown from this context; the comment implies a factor of ~40 gap unfitted, but I cannot confirm that number or how much of it Rvvs_v alone closes.

check.why: Re-runs the single fitted case and reports the ICP rise under compression, so the quoted numbers and the claimed role of Rvvs_v can be checked against current output without a full re-fit.
